_what: Paths upstream has changed since the base that the carry set ALSO modifies.
_why: verify_carry_set_applies_to_upstream_head used to require this set to be EMPTY, because an empty intersection is a sufficient condition for M6's and M10's build evidence to describe the rebased tree. It stopped being empty. Each remaining overlap has to be decided rather than tolerated, and the decision is recorded here so it can expire: the entry names the blob ids of upstream's versions of the path before and after its change, and the check refuses the entry the moment either moves. An entry can never excuse an overlap under the tree the evidence compiles - that class is rejected by verification/_carry_overlap.py before it looks at this file at all.
_maintenance: When a new overlap appears, the check FAILS and names it. Adding an entry here is a decision that the overlap does not reach either build, and it is only half the work: the reason has to be true, and the two mechanical conjuncts (outside the build tree, disjoint line regions) are checked, not read. `upstream_ranges` is the region upstream changed, as data rather than as a sentence: CARRY-LEDGER.md's `Upstream changes` column used to be scraped out of `reason` with a regex for the phrase `at base lines N..M`, so a true reason worded any other way rendered as `see below`. The check asserts the declared ranges equal the ones it computes, so this field cannot drift from the measurement either.

bootstrap.sh.reason: FOUR upstream commits have now touched this file since the base and the acknowledgement is re-derived rather than extended. 539fc58613b (`chore: remove labs-owned deploy workflows and scenario/kind/bench machinery`) removed 198 lines of `ci-network-*` arms at base lines 876..1073, which is what the previous revision of this entry recorded. Three more have landed since: 9d9523b9735 (`chore: labs submodule with a foundation patch series`), 38fd5fc6e9c (`chore!: build and test the labs components from the submodule`) and 703d8961492 (`chore!: delete the in-tree labs components`), which between them rewrite the top-level dispatch's labs-component arms in sixteen regions spanning base lines 310..1221. Patch 2 changes ONE line, base line 18, in the exported-version prologue: `expected_abs_wasi_version` 27.0 -> 33.0 plus a `WASI_SDK_PREFIX` default. Line 18 is 292 lines above the first region upstream touches, and the check computes that disjointness rather than taking this sentence's word for it.
bootstrap.sh.why_it_does_not_reach_the_build: Neither M6's AVM_WASM build nor M10's native suites execute `bootstrap.sh`. Both configure inside `barretenberg/cpp` under the fork's own `nix develop`, and the wasi-sdk they use comes from the dev shell - `verify_avm_wasm_build.sh` asserts `WASI_SDK_PREFIX` resolves into the nix store, which is the assertion that makes this more than an assumption. `bootstrap.sh`'s pin is upstream's own developer-provisioning gate; it is what patch 2 has to move for UPSTREAM's builds, and it is not an input to ours.
bootstrap.sh.consequence_if_it_stops_holding: If upstream edits the prologue this patch touches, the blobs move, this entry expires and the check goes red — and the right response is a rebase of patch 2, not a new entry. That has now happened three times WITHOUT touching the prologue, which is the entry working as designed: each time the blob moved, the entry expired, and it was re-derived against the new tip rather than widened to stop expiring.

build_root_non_inputs._what: Paths upstream has changed UNDER THE BUILD ROOT that are not build inputs. Conjunct 1 of verification/_carry_overlap.py used to be `upstream changed no path under barretenberg/cpp AT ALL`, which is a SUFFICIENT condition for M6's and M10's build evidence to describe the rebased tree and was free for six upstream moves. 38fd5fc6e9c ended it: it renames `yarn-project/` to `labs/yarn-project/` in five paths under the build root, none of which any compiler reads.
build_root_non_inputs._why: The narrowed conjunct is that no BUILD INPUT changed. The classification is COMPUTED at the tip, not listed here: `*.md` is documentation, and a `*.sh` is a non-input only if its basename appears in none of the ~128 cmake inputs under the build root, so a script an add_custom_command invokes IS a build input and reclassifies itself the day it becomes one. Anything the classifier cannot place is treated as a build input, which is the fail-safe direction. This block is the SECOND half: each surviving non-input is declared, pinned to upstream's blob ids at both ends so the entry expires the moment upstream touches the path again, and separately MEASURED to be uninvoked by M6's and M10's own build machinery — by the same spliced-in-tested invocation predicate the top-level bootstrap.sh acknowledgement uses.
build_root_non_inputs._maintenance: A new path under the build root fails the check and is named. Adding an entry here is a decision that the path is not a build input; the two mechanical conjuncts (the classifier placed it as a non-input, the blobs are current) are checked rather than read, and `upstream-changed-a-build-input` cannot be waived by anything in this file.
